intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn five small words that say how often you do things: always, usually, often, sometimes and never. You'll learn where they go in a sentence and how to ask 'How often do you …?'. Warm-up: do you drink coffee every day?
teachingNotes: Teach the five words as a scale: always (100%) > usually (about 90%) > often (about 70%) > sometimes (about 50%) > never (0%). Indonesian: selalu, biasanya, sering, kadang-kadang, tidak pernah. Don't add rarely, seldom or hardly ever yet unless the learner asks.

Position: before the main verb (I always go to the gym), but after am/is/are (She is always late). Common errors: *'I go always to the gym', *'She always is late'. Indonesian has no 'be' in 'Dia selalu terlambat', so learners put the adverb before 'is'.

Explain the jargon plainly: 'main verb' = the action word (go, eat, cook); am/is/are are not actions. A simple trick: look for am/is/are first; if there is one, the frequency word goes after it; if not, it goes before the action word. Also say why the -s stays in 'He never drinks': only do/does takes the -s away, never doesn't. Once and twice are special words (1 and 2 times); from 3 it's regular (three times). 'a week' here = per week (seminggu).

Never is already negative: *'I don't never eat meat' → 'I never eat meat'. With he/she/it the verb keeps its -s after never/always: 'He never drinks coffee' (not *'never drink', not *'doesn't never drink').

How often + do/does + subject + base verb: How often do you cook? How often does she call you? Answers: every day / every week, once a week, twice a week, three times a month, never. Once = 1 time, twice = 2 times.
In yes/no questions the adverb goes after the subject: Do you often cook? Usually and sometimes may also start a sentence (Sometimes I walk to work), but practise the middle position first.
Stay in the simple present and am/is/are: no past, future or present continuous. Use real routines: warung, kantor, sekolah, gym, mosque/church, futsal, badminton, ojek, bus.

keyPoints.title: Five words for how often
keyPoints.explanation: always (100%), usually (almost always), often (many times), sometimes (some times), never (0%). Never is already negative, so don't add don't/doesn't.

examples.en: I always get up at five.
We sometimes eat at the warung.

id.title: Lima kata untuk seberapa sering
id.explanation: always (100%), usually (hampir selalu), often (sering), sometimes (kadang-kadang), never (0%). Never sudah berarti 'tidak', jadi jangan tambah don't/doesn't.

keyPoints.title: Where the word goes
keyPoints.explanation: Put it before the main verb, the action word (I usually walk to school), but after am/is/are (He is often tired), because am/is/are aren't actions. Trick: find am/is/are first. In a do/does question, it goes after the subject, still right before the action word: Do you often cook?

examples.id: Ibu saya biasanya memasak makan malam.

examples.en: The market is always busy on Sundays.
examples.id: Pasar selalu ramai setiap hari Minggu.

id.title: Letak katanya
id.explanation: Taruh sebelum kata kerja utama, yaitu kata kegiatannya (I usually walk to school), tapi setelah am/is/are (He is often tired), karena am/is/are bukan kegiatan. Triknya: cari am/is/are dulu. Dalam pertanyaan dengan do/does, kata ini ada setelah subjek (siapa yang melakukan), tetap tepat sebelum kata kegiatannya: Do you often cook?

keyPoints.title: Asking How often …?
keyPoints.explanation: How often + do/does + subject + basic verb (no -s: cook, go). Answer with a frequency word or with every day, once a week, twice a week, three times a month. 1 time = once, 2 times = twice (special words); from 3 it's three times, four times.

examples.en: How often do you go to the gym? — Twice a week.
examples.id: Seberapa sering kamu ke gym? — Dua kali seminggu.

examples.en: How often does Sari call her mother? — Every day.
examples.id: Seberapa sering Sari menelepon ibunya? — Setiap hari.

id.title: Bertanya How often …?
id.explanation: How often + do/does + subjek + kata kerja dasar (tanpa -s: cook, go). Jawab dengan kata seberapa sering tadi, atau dengan every day, once a week, twice a week, three times a month. 1 kali = once, 2 kali = twice (kata khusus); mulai 3 jadi three times, four times.

guidedPractice.prompt: Put these words in order, from 100% to 0%: sometimes, always, never
guidedPractice.hint: Start with the word that means 'every time'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Put 'sometimes' in the right place: We eat at the warung.
expected: we sometimes eat at the warung
sometimes we eat at the warung
guidedPractice.hint: It goes before the action word (the main verb) 'eat'. Starting with Sometimes is also OK.

guidedPractice.prompt: Put 'often' in the right place: The bus is late.
guidedPractice.hint: Look for am/is/are first. There is 'is', so the word goes after is.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make a question with How often: they / go to Bandung
expected: how often do they go to bandung
guidedPractice.hint: How often + do + they + basic verb (go).

guidedPractice.prompt: Ari plays futsal on Tuesdays and Fridays. Complete: How often does Ari play futsal? — ___ a week.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one true sentence about something you never do.
independentPractice.hint: I never + verb … (no 'don't': never already means 'not').

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about your morning with 'usually'.
Ask a friend how often they watch films at the cinema.
expected: how often do you watch films at the cinema
how often do you go to the cinema
how often do you watch movies at the cinema
independentPractice.hint: How often do you …? (films/cinema is British; movies/movie theater is American. Both are fine.)

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Pak Hasan goes to the gym every day, from Monday to Sunday. Complete: Pak Hasan ___ goes to the gym.
assessment.rubric: Correct: always (every day = 100%). 'usually' = 40 (not every day). 'often' or 'sometimes' = 20. 'never' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Correct the mistake: My son doesn't never drink milk.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My son never drinks milk. 'My son never drink milk' (no -s) = 60. Keeping 'doesn't never' = 0. 'My son doesn't drink milk' = 50 (correct English but the frequency word is lost).
options: My son doesn't never drink milk.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Put 'never' in the right place: We watch TV in the morning.
assessment.rubric: Correct: We never watch TV in the morning. 'We watch never TV' or 'We don't never watch' = 0.
options: We never watch TV in the morning
We watch never TV in the morning.
We watch TV in never the morning.
assessment.correctOption: We never watch TV in the morning

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Put 'always' in the right place: Our teacher is friendly.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Our teacher is always friendly (after 'is'). 'Our teacher always is friendly' = 30.
options: Our teacher is friendly always is.

assessment.prompt: Arrange the tiles. Make a question with How often: you / play badminton
assessment.rubric: Correct: How often do you play badminton? Missing 'do' ('How often you play badminton?') = 50. 'How often are you play' = 30.
assessment.solution: how often do you play badminton

assessment.prompt: Arrange the tiles. Make a question with How often: Rina / visit her grandmother
assessment.rubric: Correct: How often does Rina visit her grandmother? 'do Rina' = 50. 'does Rina visits' = 60. Missing does = 40.
assessment.solution: how often does rina visit her grandmother

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Rina cleans her room every Saturday and on no other day. Complete the answer: How often does Rina clean her room? — ___ a week.
assessment.rubric: Correct: once (one time a week). 'one time' = 70 (understood, but 'once' is the normal word). 'twice' = 0.

blocks.text: These five words say **how often** you do something. Think of a line from 100% to 0%: **always** (every time) → **usually** (almost every time) → **often** (many times) → **sometimes** (some times) → **never** (not one time).

id.text: Lima kata ini menyatakan **seberapa sering** kamu melakukan sesuatu. Bayangkan sebuah garis dari 100% ke 0%: **always** (setiap kali) → **usually** (hampir setiap kali) → **often** (banyak kali) → **sometimes** (beberapa kali) → **never** (tidak sekali pun).

rows.en: I always get up at five.
Rina usually takes an ojek to work.
rows.id: Rina biasanya naik ojek ke kantor.

blocks.text: **Never** already means 'not', so don't add don't or doesn't: *I never eat meat*, not *I don't never eat meat* (two 'not' words in one sentence are wrong in English). With he/she/it the verb still has **-s**: *She never drinks coffee*. Why? Only **do/does** takes the -s away (*she doesn't drink*). **never** isn't do/does, so the -s stays.

id.text: **Never** sudah berarti 'tidak', jadi jangan tambahkan don't atau doesn't: *I never eat meat*, bukan *I don't never eat meat* (dua kata 'tidak' dalam satu kalimat salah dalam bahasa Inggris). Dengan he/she/it kata kerjanya tetap pakai **-s**: *She never drinks coffee*. Kenapa? Yang menghilangkan -s hanya **do/does** (*she doesn't drink*). **never** bukan do/does, jadi -s-nya tetap.

blocks.prompt: Rudi is a vegetarian. He ___ eats meat.
blocks.explain: A vegetarian eats meat 0% of the time, so: never. 'doesn't never' has two 'not' words (a double negative), which is wrong in English.

id.explain: Vegetarian makan daging 0% dari waktunya, jadi: never. 'doesn't never' punya dua kata 'tidak' (negatif ganda), dan itu salah dalam bahasa Inggris.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: Rudi is a vegetarian. He ___ eats meat.

blocks.text: Put the frequency word **before the main verb**, that is, the action word (*go, eat, walk*): *I usually walk to school.* But with **am / is / are**, put it **after**: *He is often tired.* Why? am/is/are aren't actions; they just link the person to a description. Easy trick: look for **am/is/are** first. If there is one, put the word after it. If not, put it before the action word. In a do/does question it goes after the subject, still right before the action word: *Do you often **cook**?*

id.text: Taruh kata frekuensi **sebelum kata kerja utama**, yaitu kata kegiatannya (*go, eat, walk*): *I usually walk to school.* Tapi dengan **am / is / are**, taruh **setelah**nya: *He is often tired.* Kenapa? am/is/are bukan kegiatan; kata ini hanya menghubungkan orang dengan keterangannya. Trik gampang: cari **am/is/are** dulu. Kalau ada, taruh katanya setelah itu. Kalau tidak ada, taruh sebelum kata kegiatannya. Dalam pertanyaan do/does, kata itu ada setelah subjek, tetap tepat sebelum kata kegiatannya: *Do you often **cook**?*

rows.id: Ibu saya biasanya memasak makan malam. (*cooks* = kata kegiatan)

rows.en: They often study at the library.
The market is always busy on Sundays.
rows.id: Pasar selalu ramai setiap hari Minggu. (ada *is* → always setelahnya)

rows.en: I am sometimes late for class.

blocks.text: Two common mistakes: *I go always to the gym* → **I always go to the gym**, and *She always is late* → **She is always late**. In Indonesian we say 'Dia selalu terlambat' with no 'is', so it's easy to put the word in the wrong place. **Usually** and **sometimes** can also start a sentence (*Sometimes I walk to work*), but the middle position is the safest.

id.text: Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi: *I go always to the gym* → **I always go to the gym**, dan *She always is late* → **She is always late**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang 'Dia selalu terlambat' tanpa 'is', jadi gampang salah menaruh katanya. **Usually** dan **sometimes** juga boleh di awal kalimat (*Sometimes I walk to work*), tapi posisi tengah adalah yang paling aman.

options: They go often to the mosque.
They often go to the mosque.
They often goes to the mosque.
blocks.explain: Often goes before the action word 'go', and with 'they' (more than one person) the verb has no -s.

id.explain: Often ditaruh sebelum kata kegiatan 'go', dan dengan 'they' (lebih dari satu orang) kata kerjanya tanpa -s.

blocks.text: To ask about frequency, use **How often + do/does + subject + basic verb** (no -s: *cook, go*): *How often do you cook? How often does he go swimming?* Answer with a frequency word or with **every day / every week**, **once a week** (1 time), **twice a week** (2 times), **three times a month**. Here **a week** means 'per week' (*seminggu*).

id.text: Untuk bertanya tentang frekuensi, pakai **How often + do/does + subjek + kata kerja dasar** (tanpa -s: *cook, go*): *How often do you cook? How often does he go swimming?* Jawab dengan kata frekuensi atau dengan **every day / every week**, **once a week** (1 kali), **twice a week** (2 kali), **three times a month**. Di sini **a week** artinya 'per minggu' (*seminggu*).

rows.en: How often do you go to the gym? — Twice a week.
rows.id: Seberapa sering kamu ke gym? — Dua kali seminggu.

rows.en: How often does Sari call her mother? — Every day.
rows.id: Seberapa sering Sari menelepon ibunya? — Setiap hari.

rows.en: How often do they eat out? — Once a month.
rows.id: Seberapa sering mereka makan di luar? — Sebulan sekali.

rows.en: How often do you take the train? — Never. I go by motorbike.
rows.id: Seberapa sering kamu naik kereta? — Tidak pernah. Saya naik motor.

blocks.text: **once** and **twice** are special words: 1 time = **once**, 2 times = **twice**. From 3 it's regular: **three times, four times, five times**. And after **does** the verb has no -s (*How often does Sari **call**?*), because *does* already shows he/she.

id.text: **once** dan **twice** adalah kata khusus: 1 kali = **once**, 2 kali = **twice**. Mulai dari 3 polanya biasa: **three times, four times, five times**. Lalu setelah **does** kata kerjanya tanpa -s (*How often does Sari **call**?*), karena *does* sudah menunjukkan he/she.

blocks.prompt: ___ do you go to the warung? — Every morning.
blocks.explain: 'Every morning' tells us how often, so the question is How often.

id.explain: 'Every morning' menjawab seberapa sering, jadi pertanyaannya How often.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ do you go to the warung? — Every morning.

blocks.text: Frequency words make your routine real: *I usually start work at eight. I often have lunch at a warung near the office. I sometimes work on Saturdays, but I never work on Sundays.* Ask back to keep the conversation going: *How often do you work on Saturdays?*

id.text: Kata frekuensi membuat ceritamu tentang rutinitas terasa nyata: *I usually start work at eight. I often have lunch at a warung near the office. I sometimes work on Saturdays, but I never work on Sundays.* Tanyakan balik supaya percakapan terus berjalan: *How often do you work on Saturdays?*

blocks.text: Time phrases like **every day** and **once a week** usually go at the **end** of the sentence: *I go jogging every day.* The one-word frequency words go in the **middle**: *I often go jogging.*

id.text: Frasa waktu seperti **every day** dan **once a week** biasanya ada di **akhir** kalimat: *I go jogging every day.* Kata frekuensi yang satu kata ada di **tengah**: *I often go jogging.*

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between usually and often?

Why is it 'I never eat', not 'I don't never eat'?
How do I say 'jarang' in English?
